failure_modes.description: Queue length is the primary indicator of traffic demand
failure_modes.evidence: Queue length is a lagging indicator that doesn't capture turning movements, pedestrian crossings, or future demand patterns. The system would fail to anticipate and prepare for traffic waves forming upstream.

failure_modes.description: Proportional control without integral terms will prevent oscillation
failure_modes.evidence: Control theory 101: pure proportional control guarantees steady-state error in systems with integrators. Traffic flow has inherent integrator behavior (queue accumulation), so this will必然 lead to persistent offset and oscillations.
In real networks, communication failures are common. The system doesn't specify how to handle missing neighbor data, leading to asymmetric adjustments and potential cascading failures.
Tollmien's work in 1930s and modern adaptive systems like SCATS, SCOOT, and RHODES already implement distributed coordination with more sophisticated algorithms than simple proportional control.

The falsifier condition itself exposes a critical flaw - real traffic systems must operate continuously, not have 15-minute warm-up periods. The system would cause chaos during morning rush hour while 'converging'.

failure_modes.description: Translating biological mechanisms to engineering systems
failure_modes.evidence: Myxomycetes operate on completely different timescales and physics than traffic systems. The analogy is superficial and ignores fundamental differences between biological adaptation and engineered control systems.
